title: The Notary of the Rope Bridge
story: Halfway across the Skelter Chasm, a spindly ink-stained bat-clerk unrolls a scroll longer than the bridge itself. He will not let the grain wagon pass to the hungry village of Low Thatch until the toll is paid in amber groats. Mr 6 pulls out the village charter and clears his throat politely.
question: The toll is 480 amber groats, the charter takes 25% off because the wagon carries food, and then Hexivane slaps a 10% "slow-paper fee" onto the reduced amount — how many amber groats must Mr 6 pay in all?
solution: The charter removes 25%, so the toll becomes 480 x 0.75 = 360 groats.
The slow-paper fee adds 10% of that: 360 x 1.1 = 396.
Mr 6 pays 396 amber groats and the wagon rolls on.
praise: Taking the 25% off first was the smart move — the last step was adding Hexivane's 10% onto the NEW total of 360, not the old one.
hint: Apply the discount first to get a new total, then take 10% of that new total — not of the original 480.
victory: Mr 6 counted out 396 groats in neat stacks of six, and Hexivane, finding no error anywhere, stamped the scroll so hard he fell off his own inkpot.
imagePrompt: A long-nosed, ink-stained bat-clerk in spectacles blocking a swaying rope bridge over a misty chasm, scroll unfurling into the void, while a small numeral 6 knight calmly stacks glowing amber coins on a ledger stone.
